story: I bought a second-hand auto-rickshaw for Rs 1,80,000 from a dealer in Nagpur on 14 October 2026. I drive it myself, it is how I earn my living. The engine seized after 6 days and the dealer refused to refund on 24 October 2026.

rules.name: consumer_status
rules.message: Things bought for a business usually fall outside consumer law, unless you use them only to earn your own living by self-employment. You may still have a claim in a civil court - please talk to free legal aid (15100).
rules.label: Consumer law may not apply

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 24 Oct 2028 (716 days left). This counts 2 years from 24 Oct 2026 (the date they refused; if they refused earlier, your deadline is earlier). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.
rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

answer.summary: You bought a second-hand auto-rickshaw for Rs 1,80,000 for your livelihood. The dealer refused to refund the payment. You may be able to file a consumer complaint if you use the auto-rickshaw only for self-employment. The deadline to file is before 24 October 2028. Do not wait.

claims.text: A person who buys goods for consideration, including online or offline, is a consumer.
A consumer complaint must be filed within 2 years from the date the cause of action arose.
A complaint for Rs 1,80,000 is filed with the District Commission.

support.text: A person who buys goods for consideration, including online or offline, is a consumer.
support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' as any person who 'buys any goods for a consideration' and explicitly states that 'buys any goods' includes 'offline or online transactions through electronic means or by teleshopping or direct selling or multi-level marketing'. This directly supports the sentence.

support.text: A consumer complaint must be filed within 2 years from the date the cause of action arose.
support.reason: The law text in section 69(1) states that a complaint shall not be admitted unless filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose. This directly supports the sentence.

support.text: A complaint for Rs 1,80,000 is filed with the District Commission.
support.reason: The law text in section 34(2) specifies the jurisdictional criteria for where a complaint shall be instituted (residence, business, branch office, personal work for gain, or cause of action arising, or complainant's residence), but does not specify any monetary value threshold or amount cap for filing with the District Commission. The sentence mentions Rs 1,80,000 which is not in the law text.

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.2(7) (Who is a "consumer" (with Explanation)); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation)
